battle.name: 武則天平李敬業之戰
battle.brief: 嗣聖元年（684）九月，李敬業以「匡復廬陵王」為名在揚州舉兵，旬日集眾十萬；武則天遣李孝逸將兵三十萬自洛陽沿運河東下，進逼瓜洲，叛軍部將降唐而全軍潰散。卡面羅馬重步兵非本役實物，正可對照唐軍步騎混編、全靠漕運維持的取向。

kit.name: 羅馬重步兵
kit.history: 分段鎧甲配重盾。羅馬的戰力靠的是補充兵源與補給線，不是靠重裝。

countries: 這場戰爭是唐高宗、武則天時期一場以宗室重臣為首的內亂，交戰雙方都出自唐室內部。叛軍一方是李敬業（徐敬業）所領的淮南聯軍，名義上以迎立被廢的廬陵王李顯、也就是後來的中宗為號，自稱淮南大都督，其成員主要是揚州、江都一帶召集的鄉兵、被裁汰的府兵與散卒，以及聞風而附的地方官僚與宗室舊屬，旬日之間號稱聚眾十萬；編制鬆散而無統一將令，江上舟船是其進退與運糧的關鍵，一旦被封鎖，士氣與糧秣立刻崩落。朝廷一方是武則天所主持的中央：她以右僕射李孝逸為揚州大都督，統大軍三十萬自洛陽出發，骨幹是河南、關中兩處宿衛與府兵，輔以各道州郡兵，糧食經汴渠、淮水、揚子津一路轉運，軍隊因此可以沿水路節節推進；同時遣使招撫叛軍將士，以官爵封賞勸降，瓦解其士氣。第三方是契丹：武則天令其進攻山西，令李敬業誤以為朝廷有內變，這一手成了戰局的關鍵變數；河北各州郡多持觀望，個別響應，諸說不一。
countriesEn: This war was a civil conflict inside the house of Tang in the time of Gaozong and Wu Zetian, fought between factions that both originated within the dynasty. The rebel side was the coalition of Huainan led by Li Jingye (Xu Jingye), operating under the banner of restoring the deposed Prince of Luling, Li Xian, the later Emperor Zhongzong, and styling itself Grand Commander of Huainan. Its members were chiefly levies drawn from Yangzhou and Jiangdu, demobilised fubing and loose soldiers, and local officials and old retainers of the imperial clan who answered the call; it claimed a host of one hundred thousand within ten days. Its organisation was loose, with no unified chain of command, and the boats on the river were the key to its movement and to carrying its grain: once the river was sealed, its morale and its supplies collapsed at once. The other side was the central government of Wu Zetian. She appointed the Right Vice Chancellor Li Xiaoyi as Grand Commander of Yangzhou and marched an army of three hundred thousand east from Luoyang, its backbone the imperial guards and the fubing militia of Henan and Guanzhong, supplemented by contingents drawn from the prefectures of the circuits, and its grain carried by way of the Bian Canal, the Huai River and the Yangzi Ford, so that the army could advance stage by stage along the water. At the same time envoys went out to pacify the rebel officers and men, offering ranks and rewards to those who came over, and so breaking their spirit. The third party was the Khitan: Wu Zetian had them raid Shanxi, which led Li Jingye to believe that the court itself was in disorder, and that single move became the decisive variable of the war. The prefectures of Hebei mostly watched and waited, with some of them responding; the records differ on the detail.
people: 關鍵人物集中在武則天與李敬業兩端，中間夾着一批隨局而動的朝臣與幕客。武則天是本役的決策者：她在廢中宗、立睿宗、令睿宗虛位之後，遇上李敬業以「匡復」為名的起兵，立刻調集三十萬大軍東下，又用契丹寇山西之舉擾亂李敬業的判斷，最後以招撫與進討並用收束戰局。李敬業出身顯赫，其父太尉李勣（徐世勣）為唐初第一名將，與皇室為同族遠親；他本人仕途受挫，諸史對他被貶的經過與所任職銜記載不一，或云揚州長史，或云被貶為柳州長史，怨望之下才在揚州舉兵，弟敬真與數十名宗室舊屬隨之。右僕射李孝逸是官軍主將，統兵三十萬，自洛陽沿水路東進，最後在瓜洲一線把叛軍壓垮。駱賓王為叛軍撰《為徐敬業討武曌檄》，數落武則天女主臨朝之罪，文章傳世而人亡命，後來官至武功縣丞。御史中丞蕭至忠一類言官則反對大舉用兵，主張復立中宗以安人心，此議未行。《資治通鑑》另記叛軍內部有部將夜開城門降唐之事，正是全軍崩解的關節，惟該將姓名各本記載不一。
peopleEn: The decisive figures stand at the two ends of the story, Wu Zetian and Li Jingye, with a company of courtiers and retainers drifting in between. Wu Zetian was the decision-maker of this campaign. After deposing Zhongzong, Li Xian, and setting up Ruizong, Li Dan, as a figurehead, and then changing the reign title twice in succession, to Guangzhai and to Sisheng, with all government in the hands of the empress's palace, she met a rising announced in the name of restoration, and at once brought up three hundred thousand troops, used the Khitan raid on Shanxi to confuse Li Jingye's judgement, and finally closed the affair by combining solicitation of surrender with the advance of the army. Li Jingye came from a distinguished house: his father, the Grand Commandant Li Ji (Xu Shiji), was the leading general of the early Tang and a distant kinsman of the imperial clan; the son's own career had been checked, and the histories differ on the details of his demotion and on the office he held, some making him the Changshi of Yangzhou, others a Changshi of Liuzhou degraded from his post. It was from that resentment that he raised his banner at Yangzhou, his younger brother Jingzhen and a number of old retainers of the clan going with him. The Right Vice Chancellor Li Xiaoyi was the commander of the government army: he led three hundred thousand men east from Luoyang along the water and in the end crushed the rebels on the line of the Guazhou. Luo Binwang wrote for the rebels the proclamation On behalf of Xu Jingye against Wu Zhao, setting out the empress's crimes in ruling as a woman; the piece has come down to us but its author fled for his life and was later appointed magistrate of Wugong. Officials of the censorate such as the Censor-in-Chief Xiao Zhizhong opposed a general war and urged that Zhongzong be restored to calm men's hearts, but their counsel was not taken. The Comprehensive Mirror records in addition that an officer of the rebel side opened a city gate by night and came over to the government, which was the hinge on which the whole rebel army broke up; the name of that officer is given differently in different recensions.
kits: 卡面是羅馬重步兵（Legionary），大約公元前一百年前後的羅馬軍團步兵：分段鎧甲、重盾（scutum）、長矛（pilum），全副裝備的份量遠在輕裝兵之上。684年的揚州之役與羅馬並無瓜葛，這件兵器在此只作對照之件：它代表的是「重裝步兵」這一兵種典範，而卡面那句「羅馬的戰力靠的是補充兵源與補給線，不是靠重裝」，同樣可以用來說明本役的勝負所在。唐軍這邊，護身靠兜鍪、明光鎧與札甲玄鎧，身著兩當、蔽膝與長櫜，披膊護臂齊備；兵器以長槊（步槊與馬槊）為骨，配橫刀、環首刀，射手用弓、臂弩與蹶張弩，騎兵多披甲、乘具甲馬，並有以玄甲為名的騎兵編制。攻城器械如雲梯、攻城車、撞車、飛雲，本役只見零星記載，並無大規模攻城。運輸與補給靠輜重車、糧車與大批漕船：三十萬大軍之所以能自洛陽壓到瓜洲，靠的正是汴渠、淮水、揚子津的水路，這條補給線比任何攻城器械都更能決定勝負。叛軍沒有這樣的體系，十萬眾聚在揚州一城，糧秣只靠州縣倉儲與臨時接應，因此卡面那件「靠補給線而不是靠重裝」的羅馬重步兵，恰好成了本役最切身的對照。
kitsEn: The card shows a Roman legionary of about a hundred years before the beginning of our era: the segmented armour, the heavy shield, the scutum, and the long spear, the pilum, a full kit far heavier than that of light troops. The campaign at Yangzhou in 684 has nothing to do with Rome, and this weapon appears here only as a piece of comparison: it stands for the classic type of the heavy infantryman, and the remark on the card that Roman strength rested on the replenishment of men and on the line of supply, and not on heavy equipment, applies just as well to the outcome of this war. On the Tang side the body was protected by the doumou, the bright-blaze cuirass and the plated dark armour, with a short jacket, knee guards and a long bow case, shoulder guards and arm guards complete. The weapons had the long spear, both the foot variant and the mounted one, at their core, with the straight sword and the ring-pommelled sword; the archers used bows, arm crossbows and springald-style crossbows; the cavalry were often armoured and rode armoured horses, and there was a body of horse named the Xuanjia. Siege machines such as the scaling ladders, assault cars, battering rams and the flying towers appear only sporadically here, and there is no large-scale siege to record. Transport and supply rested on baggage waggons, grain carts and a great many canal boats: the reason three hundred thousand men could press from Luoyang down to Guazhou was the waterway of the Bian Canal, the Huai and the Yangzi Ford, and that line of supply decided more than any siege engine. The rebels had no such system; a hundred thousand men crowded into the single city of Yangzhou drew their grain from the stores of the prefectures and from whatever could be got in at the time. The Roman legionary on the card, a fighting man who rested on supply rather than on weight, is therefore the closest of comparisons for this war.
tactics: 叛軍的打法是「以眾壓城」：旬日之間集眾十萬，先取濠州、滁州一帶沿江據點，分兵掠取州縣、據城以俟，把人數與地盤當成戰力，卻沒有把十萬人編成可以傳令、可以列陣的隊伍。消息面對他們致命：契丹寇山西的消息傳來，叛軍以為朝廷內變，李敬業因此鬆懈不設備，官軍得以從容布署。官軍的戰術則是「先斷其生路，再迫其出戰」：一方面遣使招撫，以官爵封賞誘降叛軍將士；另一方面三十萬大軍沿運河南下，水陸並行，先封鎖江上船隻與沿江糧道，把李敬業困在瓜洲與揚州之間的狹長地帶，再合圍進逼。叛軍後路與江防一破，士卒爭相奔竄，部將降唐，全軍在瓜洲一線崩潰，李敬業與弟敬真相繼身死於亂軍之中。整場戰役的分野很清楚：叛軍靠人數，官軍靠糧道、封鎖與時間，而人數在缺糧與喪失指揮之後，反而成了潰散的加速器。
tacticsEn: The rebels fought by trying to overwhelm the enemy with numbers. They gathered a hundred thousand men within ten days, took first the river posts of Haozhou and Chuzhou, split their force to forage across the prefectures, and sat in their towns waiting, treating numbers and ground as strength, without ever organising those hundred thousand into a body that could take an order or keep its ranks. News was fatal to them: when word came that the Khitan had raided Shanxi, the rebels took it for a sign of disorder in the capital, Li Jingye let his guard fall and made no preparation, and the government army was able to dispose itself at leisure. The method of the government army was to cut the enemy's means of life first and then force him to come out and fight. On the one hand envoys went out to solicit surrender, offering ranks and rewards to the rebel officers and men. On the other, three hundred thousand troops moved east along the water, by land and by river together, sealing first the boats on the river and the grain route along its banks, shutting Li Jingye into the narrow strip between Guazhou and Yangzhou, and only then closing in. Once the rear of the rebel position and its river defence broke, the men ran for their lives in every direction, an officer came over to the government, and the whole army came apart on the line of Guazhou, where Li Jingye and his brother Jingzhen were killed in the rout. The division between the two sides is clear: the rebels relied on numbers, the government on the line of supply, on blockade and on time, and once the grain ran out and the command was lost, the numbers themselves became the accelerant of the collapse.
data: 留下數字的地方主要在《資治通鑑》卷二百零一與《舊唐書》《新唐書》的李勣傳，但幾乎都是概數，不宜當作實帳。兵員方面，叛軍旬日之間「聚眾十萬」，這十萬包含鄉兵、被裁的府兵與散卒，以及隨軍家屬；官軍則記「將兵三十萬」，由河南、關中的宿衛與府兵為骨幹，數目與叛軍不在同一級別，且本身即是含眾多州郡之兵的概數。時間上，684年九月起兵，十一月契丹入山西，同年十二月官軍抵瓜洲、叛軍潰散，前後不過三四個月，諸說亦有作次年正月者。空間上，揚州（江都）在長江北岸，瓜洲在江都城北十餘里，與南岸揚子津隔江相望，是南北水陸的咽喉；洛陽至江都直線約六百九十公里，水路繞行則遠在千里之上，三十萬大軍的分量正壓在這段水程與沿線糧秣上。傷亡數字史無明文，只說「潰散」「為下所殺」，不宜據以推算兵員損耗；李敬業死時隨行者寥寥，也說明號稱十萬的聯軍崩散之快。
dataEn: The figures that survive are found mainly in the two hundred and first juan of the Comprehensive Mirror and in the biography of Li Ji in the Old and New Histories of Tang, but nearly all of them are approximations and should not be read as an audited account. On strength: the rebels are said to have gathered a host of a hundred thousand within ten days, and that hundred thousand covered levies, demobilised fubing and loose soldiers, and the families that followed the army. The government force is recorded as leading three hundred thousand men, with the imperial guards and the fubing of Henan and Guanzhong as its backbone, a figure of an order of magnitude above the rebels and itself a round number that folds in troops from many prefectures. In time: the rising began in the ninth month of 684, the Khitan entered Shanxi in the eleventh month, and in the twelfth month of the same year the government army reached Guazhou and the rebels came apart, three or four months from beginning to end; some accounts put the final action in the first month of the following year. In space: Yangzhou, that is Jiangdu, lay on the north bank of the Yangzi, and Guazhou was a little over ten li north of the city, facing the Yangzi Ford on the south bank across the river, the throat through which water and land passed. The straight line from Luoyang to Jiangdu runs about six hundred and ninety kilometres, and by water the road is well over a thousand, and the weight of three hundred thousand men bore down upon that stretch of water and the grain along it. There is no record of casualty figures, only of men dispersed and of men killed by their own side, and no computation of losses should be built on it; that Li Jingye was killed with only a few men about him shows how quickly the host that claimed a hundred thousand came apart.
cause: 打起來的原因是三層疊在一起。第一層是皇位交接帶來的權力真空：683年底高宗崩，中宗李顯即位旋被武則天廢，睿宗李旦被立而虛位，武則天以「光宅」「嗣聖」兩個年號連續改元，政事盡歸中宮，宗室與舊臣自居「匡復」之責，這是李敬業起兵最直接的旗號理由。第二層是李敬業本人的處境：他出身功臣之家，父李勣是唐初名將兼宗室近屬，自身仕途卻受挫被貶，懷著「失位」與「不得志」兩層怨恨，而揚州、江都一帶是他的舊治之地，號召之力遠勝他方。第三層是江南的結構性條件：隋唐以來江淮是漕運與賦稅的樞紐，州縣鄉兵舊制未廢，民間對中央的徵發與徵稅向來敏感，一旦有人以宗室之名起事，地方勢力願意以糧、兵、船資助，叛軍旬日聚眾十萬正出於此。此外朝廷自身也有判斷失誤：李敬業一旦與河北、契丹合流，後果難測，所以寧可速戰；而朝中如蕭至忠主張復立中宗、罷兵言議，終未獲採納，兵事遂不可收拾。
causeEn: The causes lie in three layers on top of one another. The first is the vacuum that came with the transfer of the throne: Gaozong died at the end of 683, Li Xian was enthroned as Zhongzong and was deposed within a few weeks, Li Dan was set up as Ruizong but remained a figurehead, and Wu Zetian changed the reign title twice in succession, to Guangzhai and to Sisheng, with all business transacted in the empress's palace. The clan and the old ministers of the Tang took on themselves the duty of restoration, and that is the banner under which Li Jingye rose. The second layer is Li Jingye's own situation: he came from a family of meritorious ministers, his father Li Ji being the first general of the early Tang and a distant kinsman of the imperial house, yet his own career had been checked and he had been demoted. He carried both the resentment of a man set aside and the frustration of a man kept down, and Yangzhou and Jiangdu were districts he knew, so his call was answered far more readily there than it would have been elsewhere. The third layer lies in the structural conditions of the south of the river: since the Sui and the Tang the Huai and the Jiang had been the hinge of transport and taxation, the militia system of the prefectures and counties had never been abolished, and the country had long been sensitive to the levies and the taxes drawn from it, so that when a man of the imperial clan raised a banner, the local forces were willing to supply men, grain and boats, and the host of a hundred thousand within ten days came out of exactly this. There was also an error of judgement at court: if Li Jingye were to join hands with Hebei and with the Khitan, the consequences could not be predicted, and so the court chose to strike at once. Proposals such as those of Xiao Zhizhong, that Zhongzong be restored and the war called off, were not adopted, and once the fighting had begun it could not be brought under control.
impact: 這場戰爭的後果超出身著本身。第一，它鞏固了武則天的權位：中宗復辟的第一次嘗試被壓了回去，此後宗室被防範更嚴，武則天對同姓諸王的防備與打擊隨之升級，690年改唐為周之前已有多位宗室被貶責，而自683年以來反覆出現的「復辟」議題自此收束，直到神龍元年（705）政變、中宗復位才算了結。第二，它把江淮與朝廷的關係推入新階段：戰後武則天對揚州、江南的財賦倚賴更深，也更倚重運河與漕運的效率，南方財賦經運河北上的格局在此役後更形固定，揚州一帶的州縣武備與鄉兵編制隨之被整頓。第三，它留下了兵制的教訓：號召十萬而無編制、糧秣不繼、指揮不一，說明唐代中晚期的州兵只適合「響應」而不適合持久作戰；而官軍三十萬沿水陸兼進、先封鎖再合圍的做法，成為此後唐廷對江南用兵的一個樣板。第四，它在文獻上留痕：駱賓王的《為徐敬業討武曌檄》成為唐代駢文傳世名篇，裡面對武則天的指斥日後反覆被引用，成為評價這位女皇的原始材料之一。史料上則要留意，本役沒有獨立的戰史，一切靠《資治通鑑》與兩《唐書》轉述，具體人名、日期與數目多有出入。
impactEn: The consequences of this war reach beyond the battlefield itself. First, it consolidated the position of Wu Zetian: the first attempt to bring Zhongzong back was pushed back, and from that point the imperial clan was watched more closely, with the empress's measures against the princes of the blood tightening in step. Before she changed the Tang to the Zhou in 690 several of the clan had already been demoted and blamed, and the theme of restoration that had come and gone since 683 was settled there and then, not to be taken up again until the coup of 705 and the second restoration of Zhongzong. Second, it carried the relationship between the court and the south of the river into a new stage: afterwards Wu Zetian leaned harder on the revenues of Yangzhou and Jiangnan, and on the efficiency of the canals and the grain traffic, so that the pattern of southern wealth moving north by water grew more fixed after this war, and the militia and the military organisation of the districts around Yangzhou were reorganised in its wake. Third, it left a lesson about military organisation. A hundred thousand men who answered a call without organisation, without continuing grain and without a single command could serve to show that the district troops of the middle and later Tang were fit for answering a rising, not for fighting a long war, while the government method of advancing three hundred thousand men by land and water together, sealing the enemy in before closing the ring, became a model for Tang campaigns in the south. Fourth, it left its mark in the written record: Luo Binwang's proclamation on behalf of Xu Jingye against Wu Zhao is a transmitted masterpiece of parallel prose in the Tang, and its indictment of the empress has been quoted again and again since, one of the original materials by which she is judged. As for the sources, one must be careful: this war has no chronicle of its own, everything survives through the Comprehensive Mirror and the two Histories of Tang, and the personal names, the dates and the figures differ in many places.
result: 結局是叛軍的徹底瓦解。官軍進逼瓜洲之後，叛軍一部降唐，江防與糧道同時崩潰，十萬眾在瓜洲一線潰散，號稱淮南大都督的李敬業與其弟敬真相繼身死（一說為部下所殺，一說自盡），諸說並存。淮南各州隨後接連歸順朝廷，武則天論功行賞，以李孝逸為首功，其餘將校各進階級，並對被裹挾的叛軍士卒與家屬寬免處置；史書又記朝廷一面懸賞捕拿，一面屢下招撫之詔，以免江南再糾結新的武裝。從朝廷的角度，這是一場乾淨俐落的完勝：即位不過數月的武則天用三十萬大軍與一場封鎖戰，消滅了第一個真正帶著宗室名號的挑戰者，睿宗的位置與中宮的權力都安然無恙。從叛軍的角度，它則是一份寫在史書裡的反叛教材：號召得十萬眾、據了揚州、拿到了名分，最後卻敗在糧秣無源、指揮不一與對形勢的誤判上——契丹入山西的消息原可成為轉機，卻先成了松懈的藉口。
resultEn: The outcome was the total disintegration of the rebel coalition. Once the government army pressed in on Guazhou, part of the rebel force came over to it, the river defence and the grain route broke down together, and the host of a hundred thousand came apart on the line of Guazhou. Li Jingye, who had styled himself Grand Commander of Huainan, and his brother Jingzhen were killed in succession, some accounts saying they were killed by their own men, others that they took their own lives, and the recensions differ. The prefectures of Huainan then returned to the government one after another. Wu Zetian rewarded the victorious commanders, putting Li Xiaoyi's work first and promoting the others by several ranks, and dealt leniently with rebel soldiers and their families who had been carried along; the histories record that the court at the same time posted rewards for the capture of the rebels and repeatedly issued proclamations of solicitation, so that the south of the river would not knot itself into a new armed rising. From the court's point of view this was a clean and complete victory: an empress who had been on the throne for only a few months destroyed, with three hundred thousand troops and a blockade, the first challenger who could put forward a genuine princely title, and neither the seat of Ruizong nor the authority of the palace was touched. From the rebels' side it is a casebook of rebellion written down in the histories: a host of a hundred thousand, the city of Yangzhou, and a name to rally under were all obtained, and in the end the rising was defeated by a want of grain, by divided command and by a misreading of the situation, for the news of the Khitan in Shanxi, which might have turned the tide, served instead as an excuse to slacken.
